title: Let greet.sh take a name
body:
### Problem

`greet.sh` always prints `Hello, world`. Callers who want to greet someone by name have to post-process its output.

### Proposed approach

In `greet.sh`, take an optional first argument and greet it instead of `world`. With no argument, the output is unchanged. Update the usage line in `README.md` to show the argument.

### Acceptance criteria

- `./greet.sh` prints `Hello, world`.
- `./greet.sh Ada` prints `Hello, Ada`.
- `README.md` shows `./greet.sh [name]`.
- No other file changes.
